title: Anaerobic respiration in muscles and in yeast
examples: What makes muscles ache after a sprint?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: No oxygen: less energy, different waste

explain.say: Imagine sprinting as hard as you can for the finish line. Your heart and lungs cannot bring oxygen fast enough. So your muscles switch to a backup plan that works without oxygen. Let's compare it with what yeast does.

draw.text: Anaerobic respiration in muscles and in yeast

draw.verdict: No oxygen: less energy, different waste

explain.say: Look at the left side: your muscles. Without enough oxygen they break glucose into lactic acid. That releases only a little energy, but fast. Anaerobic means without oxygen. When might your muscles need this backup?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: No oxygen: less energy, different waste

explain.say: Now the right side: yeast, a tiny fungus. Without oxygen it turns glucose into ethanol, a kind of alcohol, and carbon dioxide gas. This is called fermentation. Which gas do you think puffs up bread dough?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: No oxygen: less energy, different waste

explain.say: See the last line on the left. After the race you keep panting. Your body needs extra oxygen to clear the lactic acid. That is called an oxygen debt. Have you ever felt that after running?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: No oxygen: less energy, different waste

explain.say: So no oxygen means less energy and different waste. Well done! Wow fact: the holes in naan, pão and sourdough bread are bubbles of carbon dioxide made by yeast.

faq.a: During hard, fast exercise, when the blood cannot supply oxygen quickly enough. The muscles release a little extra energy without oxygen and make lactic acid.
asks: Tell me about the muscles side

faq.a: Fermentation is anaerobic respiration in yeast and some bacteria. Yeast turns glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide, releasing a little energy.
Yeast in the dough ferments sugar and gives off carbon dioxide. The gas gets trapped in the stretchy dough as bubbles, making it rise. Baking drives off the ethanol.
It is the extra oxygen your body needs after hard exercise to break down lactic acid. That is why you keep breathing fast and deep after you stop.
asks: Why do I keep panting after a race?

faq.q: Why does anaerobic respiration release less energy?
faq.a: Glucose is only partly broken down. Much energy is still locked in lactic acid or ethanol, while aerobic respiration breaks glucose all the way to carbon dioxide and water.

facts: Anaerobic respiration in human muscles produces lactic acid; in yeast it produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
Anaerobic respiration releases much less energy per glucose molecule than aerobic respiration.
